title: The unit along a finite surjective morphism is a monomorphism
statement: Let $\pi:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes which is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Then the unit $\eta_{\pi,G}:G\to\pi_*\pi^{-1}G$ of the adjunction $\pi^{-1}\dashv\pi_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is a monomorphism of $\Ab(Y_{\Et})$. (Intended proof, Stacks' argument: at a geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the stalk of $\pi_*\pi^{-1}G$ is $\prod_{\bar y'}(\pi^{-1}G)_{\bar y'}=\prod_{\bar y'}G_{\bar y}$ over the geometric points $\bar y'$ of $Y'$ with $\pi\circ\bar y'=\bar y$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction], and $\eta$ induces the diagonal map; the index set is nonempty because $Y'\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a nonempty finite $\Omega$-scheme ($\pi$ surjective) and $\Omega$ is algebraically closed; geometric stalks detect monomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono].)

source.place: Lemma 09ZE (label lemma-efface-cohomology-on-closed-by-finite-cover), proof, last paragraph (line ~14955: 'To see the desired injectivity we can look at stalks ... Since Y' -> Y is surjective and finite we see that the induced map on geometric points lifting x is surjective too'), with Proposition 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero) part (1). Stacks proves injectivity of f_*M -> f'_*M for f' = f o pi; this node is the same stalk argument for the unit along pi, from which Stacks' map is obtained by applying the left exact f_*. Reformulation by an agent.

proof.text: *The stalk of the unit is the diagonal (Stacks: '$(f_*\underline M)_{\bar x}=\bigoplus_{f(\bar y)=\bar x}M$ ... and similarly for the other sheaf').* Fix a geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ and let $P(\bar y)$ be the set of geometric points $\bar y':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'$ with $\pi\circ\bar y'=\bar y$. Write $\eta=\eta_{\pi,G}$, so $\eta(U):G(U)\to(\pi_*\pi^{-1}G)(U)=(\pi^{-1}G)(U\times_YY')$ for $U\to Y$ etale [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and let $\eta_{\bar y}:G_{\bar y}\to(\pi_*\pi^{-1}G)_{\bar y}$ be the induced map of stalks, i.e. the map of colimits over pointed etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] induced by the maps $\eta(U)$: it sends the germ of $a\in G(U)$ at $(U,\bar u)$ to the germ of $\eta(U)(a)$ at $(U,\bar u)$. For $\bar y'\in P(\bar y)$ let $r_{\bar y'}=r_{\pi,\bar y',\pi^{-1}G}:(\pi_*\pi^{-1}G)_{\bar y}\to(\pi^{-1}G)_{\bar y'}$ be the restriction of germs of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] (applied to the finite $\pi$ and $F=\pi^{-1}G$) and $c_{\bar y'}=c_{\pi,\bar y',G}:(\pi^{-1}G)_{\bar y'}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\pi\circ\bar y'}=G_{\bar y}$ the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] (applied to $f=\pi$, the geometric point $\bar y'$ of $Y'$ and its image $\bar y$). Claim: $c_{\bar y'}\circ r_{\bar y'}\circ\eta_{\bar y}=\mathrm{id}_{G_{\bar y}}$. By the universal property of the colimit $G_{\bar y}$ it suffices to check this on the germ of every $a\in G(U)$ at every pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar y$. Then: $\eta_{\bar y}$ sends it to the germ at $(U,\bar u)$ of $s=\eta(U)(a)\in(\pi_*\pi^{-1}G)(U)=(\pi^{-1}G)(U\times_YY')$; $r_{\bar y'}$ sends this, by its definition in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction], to the germ of $s$ at the pointed etale neighbourhood $(U\times_YY',(\bar u,\bar y'))$ of $\bar y'$; and $c_{\bar y'}$ sends the germ of $\eta(U)(a)$ at $(U\times_YY',(\bar u,\bar y'))$ to the germ of $a$ at $(U,\bar u)$, which is exactly the germ compatibility in the statement of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] (its $X,Y,f,\bar y,\bar x$ being our $Y,Y',\pi,\bar y',\bar y$). So the composite is the identity. Consequently, under the isomorphism $(r_{\bar y'})_{\bar y'}:(\pi_*\pi^{-1}G)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{\bar y'\in P(\bar y)}(\pi^{-1}G)_{\bar y'}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] followed by $\prod_{\bar y'}c_{\bar y'}:\prod_{\bar y'}(\pi^{-1}G)_{\bar y'}\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{\bar y'\in P(\bar y)}G_{\bar y}$, the map $\eta_{\bar y}$ becomes the diagonal $G_{\bar y}\to\prod_{P(\bar y)}G_{\bar y}$, $g\mapsto(g)_{\bar y'}$: its $\bar y'$-component is $c_{\bar y'}r_{\bar y'}\eta_{\bar y}=\mathrm{id}$. (Only the components, not the bijectivity of the product map, are used below.)

source.place: Lemma 09ZE (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-closed-by-finite-cover), proof, last paragraph, with Proposition 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero) (1) for the product decomposition and Lemma 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback) (3) for the stalk of the inverse image; Stacks states the decomposition and leaves the identification of the map implicit

proof.text: *The index set is nonempty (Stacks: 'Since $Y'\to Y$ is surjective and finite we see that the induced map on geometric points lifting $\bar x$ is surjective too').* Let $y\in Y$ be the point under $\bar y$. Since $\pi$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] there is $y'\in Y'$ with $\pi(y')=y$, and since $\pi$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-geometric-point-lift] gives a geometric point $\bar y':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'$ over $y'$ with $\pi\circ\bar y'=\bar y$, i.e. $\bar y'\in P(\bar y)$. So $P(\bar y)\neq\emptyset$.

*The stalk map is injective.* Choose $\bar y'\in P(\bar y)$ (step 2). By step 1, $c_{\bar y'}\circ r_{\bar y'}$ is a left inverse of $\eta_{\bar y}$, so $\eta_{\bar y}:G_{\bar y}\to(\pi_*\pi^{-1}G)_{\bar y}$ is injective (equivalently: the diagonal into a nonempty product is injective).

*Geometric stalks detect monomorphisms (Stacks: 'To see the desired injectivity we can look at stalks').* For every point $y\in Y$ choose an algebraic closure $\Omega_y$ of $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $\bar y_y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_y\to Y$ be the geometric point given by $y$ and $\kappa(y)\to\Omega_y$ [def-weil-geometric-point]; the family $(\bar y_y)_{y\in Y}$ covers $Y$. By steps 1-3 (applied to each $\bar y_y$) every $\eta_{\bar y_y}$ is injective, so by [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono] (the 'if' direction, for the morphism $\eta_{\pi,G}$ of $\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]) $\eta_{\pi,G}$ is a monomorphism.
